text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.5,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":1.5,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Observed: baseline 128x64x64 s1 t256 sw0 = 3560.55us; 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw64 = 3518.99us; 32x256x32 s1 t128 sw64 = 2504.88us with 330MB DRAM and 3 blocks/SM (best). Key lesson: threads=128 with the same tile/stage/swizzle nearly halved latency versus t256 (3 vs 2 blocks/SM), so thread counts are NOT cost-tied in effect despite the analytic proxy. Swizzle=64 plus narrow-M/wide-N reduced DRAM versus baseline, so panel locality shows real simulated benefit; I raise traffic weight modestly. Stage=1 dominates current tested points; I keep stages [2,3,4] to force exploration of pipelining since attempt-02/03 showed the proxy can pick s1 for every tuple, and pipeline latency reduction is untested. block_M=16 and block_N=32 are dropped as dominated survivors (too few reuses/narrow-N launches) to focus on larger tiles; block_N=256 retained (best DRAM). Weights: traffic 1.5, pipeline 1.5 to probe deeper stages, launches lowered to 0.5 since 4096^2 grid is already large, footprint 1 to stay under 32768. Constraint estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N) plus hard 32768 cap prunes oversized combos; HiGHS chooses one tuple. Scope: Metal/macOS executes exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 numbers are simulator estimates not hardware. Next hypothesis: with threads fixed to {128,256} (expect 128 wins again, confirm with different tile/stage), test stage>=2 with block_K=64/128 and swizzle>=8 to see if pipeline cost term and larger K-chunks beat the s1 wide-N config; if larger panels lose, widen swizzle weight or drop large swizzle from domain."}
